observations.text: SP, due to an incomplete working method with the performance charts of the Flight Manual, did not produce the T/O, climb, enroute, descent and landing data calculations for the planned route. The mission card was left with omissions in the leg headings and fuel figures, and the flight plan could not be filled without assistance. The IP directed the planning sequence and executed part of the enroute and descent computations. Further study of the performance charts and of the mission card format is required.

SP, due to mission planning that did not address the forecast weather at the recovery time, did not review the applicable NOTAMS and did not select alternate airfields for the route. The briefing was delivered with omissions in the required conditions and restrictions, and the SP could not establish the go/no-go picture unaided. The IP had to direct the weather and NOTAM review and to nominate the alternates before the sortie could be flown.

SP planned the mission and executed the briefing and debriefing at the standard required for this stage. Two turning-point time and fuel figures were entered on the mission card only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the plotted route was corrected with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section - independent use of the aeronautical maps and MAIP during planning is expected to improve.

SP planned the mission IAW the Squadron's Tactical Standards and completed the T/O, climb, enroute, descent and landing calculations without IP prompting. Minor errors in two leg headings on the mission card were recognized and corrected in a timely manner by the SP, without IP's intervention. The briefing and the debriefing were executed without omissions. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the mission accurately and rapidly, plotting the route on the map correctly and selecting significant ground references for every leg. Performance charts, aeronautical maps and MAIP were used with proficiency, and the mission card and the flight plan were filled without omissions. Alternate airfields were chosen and heading, time and fuel to the nearest airfield were planned at every turning point. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the mission to a standard well above that required at this stage, cross-referencing the Flight Manual performance charts, MAIP, FLIPs and AFMAN 11-202 VOL3 without a single omission on the mission card or the flight plan. Ground reference selection per leg and the turning-point diversion data - heading, time and fuel to the nearest airfield - showed negligible deviation from the check figures, and the briefing and debriefing were delivered to instructional standard. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a disordered planning sequence in which the route was plotted before the weather and the NOTAMS were reviewed, did not identify a restriction affecting the second leg and did not revise the flight altitude selection. The mission card was presented with the enroute and descent calculations incomplete. The IP directed the re-plot and executed part of the fuel planning to the alternate airfields.

SP, due to failure to identify a known threat during mission planning, did not brief the applicable restrictions and did not nominate alternate airfields for the middle legs of the route. The debriefing omitted the deviations that had been recorded in flight. The IP had to lead both the missing briefing items and the debriefing sequence for the event to be completed.

SP, due to an unpracticed working method with the Flight Manual performance charts, did not complete the climb and enroute calculations at the first attempt and did not select significant ground references for two legs. The mission card was finished only after the IP's verbal prompts and the omissions were recognized and corrected with delay. The route plot and the flight plan were otherwise correct.

SP, due to lack of awareness of a published restriction that was available in the briefing material, did not incorporate the restriction into the flight altitude selection and did not cover it during the briefing. The point was raised and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, and the mission card and flight plan were amended with delay. The debriefing thereafter addressed the item without further assistance.

SP planned the mission and delivered the briefing and debriefing within the desired standards for this stage. Two turning-point fuel figures were computed with minor errors, both recognized and corrected by the SP without IP's intervention, and one alternate airfield was nominated only on the second review of the route. Marginal performance for the Training Section - accuracy of the turning-point diversion data is expected to improve.

SP planned the mission accurately and rapidly IAW the Squadron's Tactical Standards, with the T/O, climb, enroute, descent and landing calculations complete and correct. The route was plotted correctly, significant ground references were selected per leg, and the mission card and the flight plan were filled without omissions. Briefing and debriefing were executed without omissions and without IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP planned the mission with exceptional accuracy, using the Flight Manual performance charts, aeronautical maps, MAIP and FLIPs at a level above that required at the end of the block. Alternate airfields and the heading, time and fuel to the nearest airfield at every turning point were computed with negligible deviation from the check figures, and the debriefing identified the SP's own deviations before the IP raised them. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect application of the Flight Manual performance charts, did not produce usable enroute and landing data and did not complete the fuel planning to the alternate airfields. The route plot did not agree with the mission card headings on two legs. The IP directed the recomputation and executed part of the descent and landing calculations before the briefing could proceed.

SP, due to planning conducted without the current publication for the route, did not verify the enroute restrictions or the alternate airfield data against the MAIP. The mission card was completed from superseded information and the briefing did not cover the actual conditions and restrictions in force. The IP had to interrupt the briefing, direct the SP to the current publications and execute part of the re-planning.

SP, due to a slow and non-standardized use of the aeronautical maps, did not select significant ground references for three legs and did not complete the turning-point time and fuel entries on the mission card. The entries were made only after the IP's verbal prompts and the route plot was corrected with delay. The briefing was otherwise delivered in the prescribed sequence.

SP, due to complacency on a route flown repeatedly without incident, did not re-check the NOTAMS and the current weather before the briefing and did not revise the alternate airfield selection. The omission was recognized and corrected only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the flight plan amended with delay. The remaining planning items and the debriefing were correct.

SP, due to a hurried cross-check of the Flight Manual performance charts, extracted the enroute fuel flow for the wrong pressure altitude and produced two turning-point fuel figures in error. The SP identified the discrepancy while reviewing the mission card and recomputed the figures correctly before the briefing, in a timely manner and without IP's intervention. The route plot, the ground reference selection and the flight plan were otherwise complete.

SP, due to distraction by a secondary task during the planning phase, omitted the diversion data for the third turning point when filling the mission card. The omission was detected by the SP on the self-review before the briefing and the heading, time and fuel to the nearest airfield were completed without IP's intervention. The briefing and the debriefing were executed without omissions.

SP planned the mission with proficiency IAW the Squadron's Tactical Standards and executed the briefing and the debriefing without omissions. Two enroute fuel figures required a second computation before the briefing, and the debriefing needed IP prompting to reach the causes rather than the symptoms of the in-flight deviations. Marginal performance for the Training Section - speed of the data calculations and depth of self-analysis in the debriefing are expected to improve.

SP planned the mission to a standard above that required at the end of the block, with all T/O, climb, enroute, descent and landing calculations verified against the Flight Manual charts and negligible deviation from the check figures. Route plot, ground reference selection per leg, alternate airfields and the turning-point heading, time and fuel data were complete and precise, and the mission card and flight plan carried no omissions. The debriefing was structured and self-critical and identified every significant deviation before the IP raised it. Above end of block MIF achieved.
